description: Card P's targets for "Small-block 5.7 L, carburettor-like": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 8/2, 46.7 Hz at the 700 rpm idle and 367 Hz at the 5500 rpm limiter; each bank fires unevenly, so half-order lines (23.3 Hz at idle) stand out from a single bank's pipe.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a rev limiter holds the speed within a few percent of where it cuts (some 100 to 200 rpm at 6500)

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor in third of eighteen at least 1.5 m/s)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (net ratings of the era, loose): 4.00 x 3.48 in: 101.6 x 88.4 mm, 5733 cc; 24 to 37 kW a litre

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (net ratings of the era, loose): 4.00 x 3.48 in: 101.6 x 88.4 mm, 5733 cc: 4000 to 5200 rpm

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (net ratings of the era, loose): 4.00 x 3.48 in: 101.6 x 88.4 mm, 5733 cc; BMEP 8.3 to 10.3 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2)

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (net ratings of the era, loose): 4.00 x 3.48 in: 101.6 x 88.4 mm, 5733 cc: 2400 to 3600 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span)

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 600 to 800 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 700

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb); a lope of more than 150 rpm over the range's top is a fault

targets.name: Volumetric efficiency at its torque peak
targets.source: a naturally aspirated four-stroke's VE at full load near its torque peak is 0.85 to 1.0 (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 6, fig. 6-9 and the text); measured at 4000 rpm

targets.name: Volumetric efficiency low down
targets.source: VE's shape: below the torque peak it falls away, the more so the hotter the cam (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 6); measured at 2000 rpm

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: the gas at the exhaust valve at full load, before the port and pipe cool it: some 1100 to 1300 K for a spark-ignition engine (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14; card C's target on default.json, which this follows)

targets.name: Header gas at full load
targets.source: a thermocouple a little way down a primary reads 900 to 1100 K at full load on a petrol engine (makers' exhaust-gas-temperature data; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14); n/a until the exhaust reports it

targets.name: Quarter mile: time
targets.source: Hale's rule, ET = 5.825 (lb/hp)^(1/3) s, with the kind's published power (175 kW) and the build's mass: 14.38 s; 5 % quicker to 15 % slower for the build's own tyres and launch (card I's test holds drag radials to 8 %)

targets.name: Quarter mile: trap speed
targets.source: Hale's rule, trap = 234 (hp/lb)^(1/3) mph: 42.4 m/s (153 km/h), within 8 % under to 6 % over

targets.name: Top speed
targets.source: the redline in top gear with the build's gearing: 199 km/h, within 7 % (geared, not drag-limited); no speed governor is simulated
